title: Tasks, Priorities, and Scheduling knowledge check

questions.prompt: What is the most direct learning goal for this lesson?
options: Use tasks, priorities, and scheduling only for visual styling.
Skip type checking and accept any result.
Replace a focused example with unrelated code.

questions.answer_key: The main goal is to apply task priorities in a small Swift example and verify the result.
questions.explanation: Tasks, Priorities, and Scheduling is best learned through a small, verifiable example. Asynchronous execution can suspend while work waits; it is not automatically the same as parallel execution. Design cancellation, error propagation, task lifetime, and shared-state isolation deliberately.
